# gns3_template (Resource)

A user template on the GNS3 controller, for `gns3_node.template_id`. Built-in templates (VPCS, Ethernet switch, ...) can't be managed or imported; read them with the `gns3_template` data source. Destroying the template does not affect nodes already created from it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A user VPCS template. properties holds the type-specific fields; only the
# keys set here are compared with the server.
resource "gns3_template" "pc" {
  name          = "tf-example-vpcs"
  template_type = "vpcs"
  properties    = jsonencode({ console_type = "telnet" })
}

# A qemu template for an appliance disk image already on the compute (see
# gns3_image). Creating the template does not start anything.
resource "gns3_template" "router" {
  name          = "tf-example-qemu"
  template_type = "qemu"
  properties = jsonencode({
    ram            = 512
    adapters       = 3
    platform       = "x86_64"
    hda_disk_image = "vyos-1.4.qcow2"
  })
}

resource "gns3_project" "lab" {
  name = "tf-example-template"
}

# Nodes take the template's template_id like a built-in's.
resource "gns3_node" "pc1" {
  project_id  = gns3_project.lab.project_id
  template_id = gns3_template.pc.template_id
  name        = "PC1"
  x           = 0
  y           = 0
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Template name. GNS3 allows two templates with the same name. Changed in place.
- `template_type` (String) Emulator type: one of `cloud`, `nat`, `ethernet_hub`, `ethernet_switch`, `docker`, `dynamips`, `vpcs`, `traceng`, `virtualbox`, `vmware`, `iou`, `qemu`. Changing it replaces the template (GNS3 2.2 accepts a new type in an update but ignores it).

### Optional

- `compute_id` (String) Compute that nodes from this template run on. Default `local`. Changing it replaces the template (GNS3 2.2 accepts a new compute in an update but ignores it).
- `properties` (String) Type-specific template fields as a JSON object (use `jsonencode`), for example `{ ram = 512, adapters = 2, hda_disk_image = "vyos.qcow2" }` for `qemu`. Only the keys you set are compared with the server, so the defaults GNS3 fills in do not show as drift. `dynamips` needs `platform` and `image`, and `docker` needs `image`. The common fields (`template_id`, `name`, `template_type`, `compute_id`, `category`, `symbol`, `builtin`, `default_name_format`) are refused here. A change is applied in place. GNS3 2.2 does not check type-specific keys in an update, so the provider first creates a throwaway copy named `tf-validate-<random>` with the new properties, which GNS3 does check, and deletes it again. A key you remove from the configuration keeps its value on the server, because a GNS3 update merges keys.

### Read-Only

- `builtin` (Boolean) Always `false`: built-in templates are refused.
- `category` (String) `router`, `switch`, `guest` or `firewall`, as filled in by the server for the template type.
- `default_name_format` (String) Node name pattern, for example `PC{0}`, as filled in by the server for the template type.
- `symbol` (String) Symbol path, as filled in by the server for the template type.
- `template_id` (String) Template UUID assigned by the server, for `gns3_node.template_id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by template_id. Built-in templates are refused.
terraform import gns3_template.pc 5bb744cc-7ef9-49c0-a50a-c383d00bf3d5
```
